AMZN.rationale: Amazon presents a solid fundamental case with accelerating growth and strong competitive positioning, tempered by elevated valuation and near-term cash flow pressure from massive capex. The company's Q1 2026 results were exceptional: revenue of $181.5B (+17% YoY), EPS of $2.78 crushing consensus of $1.65, and a record operating margin of 13.1%. AWS reaccelerated to 28% growth (fastest in 15 quarters) with AI revenue at a $15B annualized run rate. The custom chip business (Trainium/Graviton) is growing at triple-digit rates with a $225B backlog. Advertising revenue now exceeds $70B trailing four quarters at ~80% incremental margins, on track for $90B by 2027. However, the stock trades at a P/E of 38x, near the top of its 365-day range (28-39x), and P/B of 7.9x is also elevated. The $200B 2026 capex plan has crushed free cash flow to just $1.2B (down 95% YoY), creating legitimate investor concern. Balance sheet remains strong with $369.6B equity and only $55B debt (D/E 0.15). The quarterly trajectory shows accelerating revenue and EPS growth (Q1 $155.7B/$1.59 → Q2 $167.7B/$1.68 → Q3 $180.2B/$1.95). Near-term catalysts include Nvidia earnings (May 20) which could validate or challenge the AI capex thesis, and Amazon's own Q2 guidance of $194-199B revenue. Macro headwinds are notable: 10Y Treasury at 4.57%, oil at $100/bbl, and rising inflation concerns. News sentiment is moderately positive (mean 0.335 over 90 days). Berkshire Hathaway exited its Amazon position in Q1 2026, while Bill Ackman and David Tepper added to theirs, reflecting mixed institutional views. The FTC antitrust trial in October 2026 and EU regulatory pressure represent ongoing overhangs. Overall, strong fundamentals and trajectory support a positive view, but the stock is not cheap versus its own history, capping the score.

Amazon stock surged 27.3% in April and continued climbing in May, driven by a major chip deal with Meta Platforms and better-than-expected Q1 earnings. The company reported $2.78 EPS and $181.52B revenue, beating analyst expectations. AWS revenue grew 28% YoY to $37.59B
Amazon's custom AI chip business is experiencing explosive growth with a $225 billion revenue backlog and triple-digit year-over-year growth. The company's Trainium3 chips are nearly sold out
Amazon is discontinuing its Rufus chatbot and replacing it with Alexa for Shopping, a new AI-powered shopping assistant
Berkshire Hathaway completely exited its Amazon position in Q1 2026, selling its remaining shares after holding 10 million shares in September 2025
Billionaire investor David Tepper's Appaloosa fund made significant AI-focused investments in Q1 2026: nearly doubling its Amazon stake
Bill Ackman's Pershing Square Capital Management significantly increased positions in Microsoft and Amazon during Q1 2025
Trailing free cash flow fell to $1.2 billion from $25.9 billion, a 95 percent drop. Operating cash flow rose 30 percent to $148.5 billion, but nearly all incremental cash is being reinvested

AWS segment revenue climbed 28% year-over-year to $37.6 billion, marking the fastest growth rate in over three years. Operating income rose to $23.9 billion, delivering a record operating margin of 13.1%
Amazon's advertising segment has now generated more than $70 billion in revenue over the trailing four quarters, growing at a 24% year-over-year clip. Incremental margins in the neighborhood of 80%
Amazon's free cash flow has significantly deteriorated, collapsing 95% year-over-year to $1.2 billion in Q1 2026, while long-term debt nearly doubled to $127.3 billion
AMZN key risks include escalating global regulatory scrutiny targeting its marketplace and labor practices, and significant pressure on profitability from massive investments
